newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adtranz says to join Transrapid consortium.
newsitem.headline: Adtranz says to join Transrapid consortium.

text.p: Adtranz, the rail joint venture between Daimler-Benz and ABB, on Friday confirmed that it would be joining the consortium building the nine billion marks ($5.2 billion) Transrapid railway project.

Eckhard Cordes, Daimler management board member and chairman of the Adtranz supervisory board, confirmed an earlier announcement by German Transportation Minister Matthias Wissmann that Adtranz would be joining the consortium.
"With our participation in (the Transrapid project) we will use the opportunity to maintain and expand our leading role in the German rail industry," said Cordes.
Adtranz's involvement comes as part of a new financing and management structure for Transrapid announced by Wissmann in Bonn earlier in the day.

His comments came in the wake of news from German construction group Philipp Holzmann AG which said that the construction groups in the Hamburg-Berlin rapid rail scheme would be leaving the consortium set up to design and build the Transrapid rail project.
Holzmann told Reuters that the Transrapid consortium considered the costs associated with itself, and fellow builders Hochtief AG and Bilfinger+Berger AG were too high.
The three builders had however seen no room to reduce costs to the extent demanded by the other partners in the consortium.

The Transrapid project, which uses magnetic levitation technology, has come under criticism both as to whether there is sufficient demand for it in Germany and whether it can justify the six billion marks of state funding Bonn plans to offer for it.
